preamble: Between vowels, the voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] lenited to a retroflex lateral [ɭ]. The tongue keeps its curled-back position, but the full closure is replaced by lateral airflow.

examples.note: Rigveda 1.1.1 'agním īḷe' ('I praise Agni'): the intervocalic ḍ is written and recited as ḷ (the Rigvedic form), while the later standard text has ḍ.
Sanskrit krīḍ- 'to play': the intervocalic ḍ appears as ḷ in Pali.

sources: Burrow, T. (1955). The Sanskrit Language. Faber & Faber.
Geiger, W. (1916). Pāli Literatur und Sprache. Trübner.
Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
